messages:
mira: quick question — sim surfaced a weird edge case: affinity routing kept routing to eu-west GPUs even after spot prices spiked and latency climbed. the request window overlapped the price update. how do we want tie-breakers to behave when cost signals change mid-decision?

dan: is this the sim harness or replayed prod traces?

mira: replayed prod traces from last night + sim that tries to model rapid price blips. not a full outage, just oscillation for a few seconds.

joey: my gut: once a route is selected for an in-flight request, it should be sticky for the lifetime of that request. otherwise we risk inconsistent KV cache/state and increased tail latency.

priya: strong +1 on stickiness for in-flight. but for new requests we should prefer the cheaper route once we detect sustained cost change. need to define "sustained" though.

leo: leaning toward a two-tier rule: hard constraints (region/compliance) always immutable; soft penalties (cost/latency) influence selection for new requests only unless the change is catastrophic (e.g., latency > SLO*3 or node unhealthy).

sasha: agree. also we should add a short preemption window where we allow new requests to be steered off high-cost nodes before we drain in-flight. like a 5s quiesce period.

mira: concrete asks: (1) policy order (hard vs soft) clarified, (2) define stickiness semantics, (3) decide preemptive window and telemetry staleness tolerances.

dan: for (2) we already have request_id pinning in the router. pinning prevents mid-flight reroute. we just need to codify that in policy docs.

priya: for (1) propose this evaluation order: 1) compatibility/hard constraints, 2) capacity & health filters, 3) penalty scoring (cost/latency/region-preference), 4) deterministic tie-breaker (hash/request-id). That keeps deterministic behavior.

joey: deterministic tie-breaker should be stable across instances. use tenant_id + route_salt + request_id fallback. makes replay/debugging easier.

leo: for (3) telemetry staleness — we should treat price-like signals with higher smoothing and a min-observation window (e.g., 30s) before changing routing weights. latency signals can be faster but still require a hysteresis to avoid thrash.

mira: sounds reasonable. one more: private deployments can have only one region/cluster — fallback semantics differ. if tenant has no compatible fallback, we should avoid steering by cost alone.

sasha: yes — add a tenant capability flag: allow_cross_region_fallback = true|false. if false, cost penalties are capped and do not trigger cross-region change.

priya: example config snippet for discussion:
```json
{
  "penalty_decay_ms": "60000",
  "price_signal_window_ms": "30000",
  "inflight_stickiness": "true",
  "preemptive_quiesce_s": "5",
  "max_cross_region_penalty": "0.25"
}
```

joey: nit: use ms for consistency. make default penalty_decay 120000ms for hosted to avoid rapid oscillation.

mira: ops implications: what do oncall playbooks look like if a pricing provider goes noisy? ops-bot any suggestions?

ops-bot: if external price feed is noisy mark feed as degraded and switch to smoothed/median signal. emit alert when feed variance > threshold for > 2 mins.

leo: also we should add a simulation test for mid-window spikes that asserts in-flight requests stay pinned and new requests respect preemptive_quiesce. add to policy-sim test matrix.

mira: agreed — i'll add tests. final decision checklist: codify evaluation order (hard->health->penalties->tie-breaker), enforce in-flight stickiness by request_id, introduce preemptive_quiesce default 5s, require price_signal_window >= 30s for price inputs, and tenant flag for cross-region.

priya: can we also add a metric: "route_flip_rate" per tenant to detect thrash? alert if > X flips/min.

leo: great idea. add to console dashboards.

mira: thanks all. i'll draft a short RFC follow-up with the config defaults and sim results. tagging @joey for deterministic tie-breaker impl and @sasha for ops playbook. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rollout scheduled: policy-engine v2.3.1 -> canary (5%) at 2026-03-22T02:00Z

joey: will pick up implementation. planning small migration: policy hotreload to respect new fields without restart.

mira: perfect. closing thread once RFC is in PR.
